bib.title: JIT-Agent: Scaling Harness Intelligence via Just-in-Time Harness Evolution

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "JIT-Agent: Scaling Harness Intelligence via Just-in-Time Harness Evolution", JIT-Agent Team (core: Guibin Zhang, Leo Lu, Fangzhou Xie; corresponding incl. Wangchunshu Zhou, Shuicheng Yan; NUS, EverMind AI, NTU), arXiv:2608.25593v2 (cs.CL), 3 Sep 2026. Preprint. Code: github.com/bingreeky/JIT

COVERAGE: All 24 pages, 72,213 chars. Main text, Tables 1-4, appendices A-C read in full. Reference list (about pp. 11-16) only skimmed. Extraction is clean text; figures are image-only (diagram text partly lost).

CLAIMS (ranked)
- claim: Replacing the default scaffold with a JIT-generated harness improved all 18 matched backbone-benchmark pairs. Average rose by 7.7 on GLM-5.2 and 8.8 on DeepSeek-V4-Flash.
  number: 74.1 to 81.8 (GLM-5.2); 66.7 to 75.5 (V4-Flash)
  setup: 9 benchmarks, 4 task types, 0-100 scale. The baseline is each vanilla model with its default scaffold (not a named ReAct run).
  quote: "Replacing the default scaffold improves all 18 matched backbone–benchmark pairs: the average score rises from 74.1 to 81.8 on GLM-5.2 (+7.7) and from 66.7 to 75.5 on DeepSeek-V4-Flash (+8.8)."
  where: p.8, Sec 5.2
- claim: With the backbone held fixed, JIT-generated harnesses are competitive with Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Hermes and NanoBot. They also use the fewest tokens and the lowest cost in all six settings.
  number: best performance in 4 of 6 settings; cost cut 14.9-54.1% vs the cheapest fixed harness, 36.0% on average
  setup: DeepSeek-V4-Flash and Qwen3.6-Flash; DeepSearchQA, xBench-DS, AgentIF; per-case tokens and USD. Not a pass on the other two: it trailed by 3.1 and 3.9 points.
  quote: "JIT-Agent has the lowest token consumption and cost in all six settings, reducing per-case cost by 14.9–54.1% relative to the cheapest fixed alternative, or 36.0% on average."
  where: pp.8-9, Sec 5.3 and Table 3
- claim: Example from Table 3. On V4-Flash xBench-DS the JIT harness cut tokens and cost and raised the score.
  number: 527K to 212K tokens; $0.075 to $0.039; 78.0 to 82.0
  setup: vs NanoBot, the best fixed harness, on that benchmark
  quote: "On DeepSeek-V4-Flash xBench-DS, it cuts tokens from 527K to 212K and cost from $0.075 to $0.039 while raising performance from 78.0 to 82.0"
  where: p.9
- claim: Fixed harness rankings are not stable across tasks. In Table 3, OpenCode is the most expensive harness in every column.
  number: e.g. OpenCode 1,832K tokens, $0.258 on DSQA with V4-Flash
  setup: Table 3
  quote: "OPENCODE75.9 1,832 $0.258"
  where: p.8, Table 3
- claim: A small open model with a JIT harness beats a frontier model on some benchmarks. JIT-equipped systems lead 8 of 9 columns. JIT+GLM-5.2 ranks first on 7.
  number: +9.1 DeepSearchQA and +4.3 OdysseyBench (V4-Flash vs GPT-5.6); GLM-5.2 gains up to +20.2
  setup: Table 2; the gap to GPT-5.6 is measured against vanilla GPT-5.6. The DeepSeek-V4-Flash row has DSQA 85.1 vs GPT-5.6 76.0.
  quote: "DeepSeek-V4-Flash surpasses GPT-5.6 by 9.1 points on DeepSearchQA and 4.3 on OdysseyBench, while GLM-5.2 gains up to 20.2 points."
  where: p.3, Sec 1 and Table 2 (p.8)
- claim: Gains are largest on long-horizon planning. DeepPlanning-Travel is the one column where JIT did not lead.
  number: +24.8 Shopping (V4-Flash, 59.1 to 83.9); +20.2 Travel (GLM-5.2, 62.8 to 83.0); Travel within 1.9 of GPT-5.6
  setup: Table 2
  quote: "+24.8 on DeepPlanning-Shopping for DeepSeek-V4-Flash (59.1→83.9) and +20.2 on DeepPlanning-Travel for GLM-5.2 (62.8→83.0)"
  where: p.8
- claim: The harness transfers across model families. JIT beats a fixed ReAct harness on 24 of 24 comparisons.
  number: +7.6 average; family gains 10.2 (DeepSeek V4), 4.0 (Qwen3.6), 8.6 (Mimo-V2.5); DSQA +15.2 average
  setup: 6 backbones, 4 benchmarks. Small subsets: DeepSearchQA 100 examples, the other three 50 examples each (Fig 4 caption).
  quote: "JIT-Agent wins all 24 matched comparisons by 7.6 points on average, with family-level gains of 10.2, 4.0, and 8.6 points, respectively."
  where: p.10, Sec 5.5; Fig 4 caption p.9
- claim: Streaming mode, where the harness bank is updated from execution feedback with no weight updates, ends above static mode on all three streams. The paper gives no numbers, only curves.
  number: none
  setup: DeepPlanning-Shopping, DeepPlanning-Travel, OfficeBench (Fig 6); cost and tool calls "broadly similar scale"
  quote: "Streaming JIT finishes above the static variant on DeepPlanning-Shopping, DeepPlanning-Travel, and OfficeBench."
  where: p.17, App B.1
- claim (the part that matters for the anatomy note): The paper factors a harness into four modules, h=(M,P,A,F). Memory is how history is compressed into a view. Planning forms a local directive. Capability orchestration (F) picks which tools and skills are active. Action updates controller state and emits the next action. Runtime dependency order is M→P→F→A.
  number: none (13 seed harnesses in Table 1)
  setup: "protocol" Π with fixed module schemas. Existing harnesses map into it: ReAct = full-history memory, no planner, ReAct action, full registry. Codex and OpenCode = compact memory plus todo planning. ROMA, AOrchestra and RLM = recursive.
  quote: "at runtime, its dependency order is M→P→F→A" and "canonical ReAct uses full-history memory, no explicit planner, a ReAct loop, and the full capability registry"
  where: p.4, Sec 3.1
- claim: Training recipe (Qwen3.6-27B base): Stage I is SFT plus DPO on teacher-generated, validated harnesses. Preferences require higher reward with no latency or cost regression. Stage II is repair, trained only on failures that become executable within two rounds. Stage III is Evo-GDPO, with reward, latency and cost advantages normalized separately. Reward weight is greater than the latency weight plus the cost weight. Efficiency counts only if incumbent reward is preserved. The bank keeps a candidate only if it matches or beats the frontier and strictly improves one dimension.
  number: K0=13 seeds; repair ≤2 rounds; 3 reference scaffolds per task in Stage I
  setup: generator is frozen at deployment. Static inference generates N harnesses and runs only the selected one.
  quote: "We retain only trajectories that become executable within two rounds"
  where: pp.5-7, Sec 4
- claim: Generated harnesses are task-shaped, not prompt variants. Appendix C describes nine, for example: a bounded 5-step research subagent with a fact-graph memory (Trapdoor); a final_answer tool withheld until is_complete() passes (Turnstile); a phase register that swaps tools and memory schema (Gearbox); a candidate-by-clue evidence matrix with doc IDs (Pegboard); full history stored but only first, last and top-K observations rendered (Appraiser); computation moved to code with typed RESULT_JSON state (Abacus); per-file deterministic non-LLM verification (Player Piano); narrow tool exposure plus step retry limited to 2 attempts (Mulligan).
  number: none
  setup: qualitative case studies, no ablation
  quote: "DynamicToolPolicy exposes search tools for the missing bucket but withholds final_answer until is_complete() succeeds."
  where: pp.19-23, App C
- claim: Contrast with prior work. Meta-Harness, AHE and AutoHarness search ahead of time. Adaptive AH, TTHE and RHI edit a harness at test time. Harness-R1 has a trained model, learned repair and online evolution but is still AOT. JIT-Agent is the only one marked for instance synthesis.
  number: none
  quote: "JIT-Agent (ours) JIT✓ ✓ ✓ ✓"
  where: p.17, Table 4. The comparison is structural, not empirical.

LIMITS
- There is no ablation of Stages I-III in the extracted text, and no per-module analysis of which of M/P/A/F drives the gains. Gains are attributed to "task-conditioned scaffolds" without a controlled test.
- Fig 4 uses 50-100 example subsets. No variance, seeds or confidence intervals are reported.
- Table 3 covers 3 benchmarks and 2 backbones. The harness comparison does not cover the other six benchmarks.
- The "vanilla" baselines use each model's own default scaffold, so the gain figures mix harness and scaffold differences. The numbers for GPT-5.6, Gemini and others are single runs as reported.
- The generator is trained on tasks from the same benchmark families it is evaluated on, plus synthesized tasks. Train and test overlap is not discussed in the text read.
- The cost of running JIT-Agent-27B itself (generation, repair) is not reported separately in the extracted text. Table 3 per-case cost may or may not include it.
- The paper does not state limitations in a dedicated section.
- Table 4 is the authors' own classification of competitors.

BUILDS ON: ReAct (Yao et al., 2023a). Harness optimization lines: Meta-Harness (Lee et al., 2026c), AHE (Lin et al., 2026), AutoHarness (Lou et al., 2026), TTHE (Nie et al., 2026), RHI (Lee et al., 2026a), Harness-R1 (Shao et al., 2026), Adaptive AH (Liu et al., 2026b). Earlier prompt and workflow optimization (Khattab et al., 2023; Yuksekgonul et al., 2024; Hu et al., 2024b; Shang et al., 2024). Harness definition (Meng et al., 2026b; Zhou et al., 2026). Evo-GDPO is "inspired by (Liu et al., 2026a)", with GDPO/GRPO and PPO. The 13 seed harnesses: ReAct, Plan-and-Execute, ReSum, Flash-Searcher, GAM, MemoBrain, AggAgent, OAgent, AgentFold, HiAgent, DeepAgent, ROMA, AOrchestra. "Code carries the harness" (Ning et al., 2026; Pan et al., 2026).

CODE: None as code. The load-bearing formulas are in Sec 3.1 (Eq. 3, p.4): v_t = M(ξ_<t, s_t); d_t = P(τ, s_t, v_t); C_t = F(C_τ, s_t, v_t, d_t); (s_{t+1}, e_t) = A(s_t, τ, v_t, d_t, C_t). Also the preference rule (Eq. 4, p.6).

FIGURES (captions only; not rendered)
- Fig 1 (p.2): overview, with the four modules instantiated per task for deep research, product generation and autonomous research. Quick picture of the M/P/A/F decomposition.
- Fig 2 (p.5): the three-stage training pipeline.
- Fig 3 (p.9): cost vs performance Pareto frontier for DSQA and AgentIF. Shows the leftward cost shift.
- Fig 4 (p.9): ReAct vs JIT across 6 backbones, 4 benchmarks, with paired bars.
- Fig 5 and C.1-C.9 (pp.10, 18-23): generated harness diagrams. The most useful for the anatomy note are C.3 (gated final_answer), C.6 (render top-K only) and C.9 (transactional step retry).
- Fig 6 (p.18): streaming vs static cumulative accuracy, cost and tool calls.
- Table 1 (p.5): inventory of the 13 seeds by M/P/A/F. Table 4 (p.17): optimization paradigms.

PROBLEMS: None blocking. No embedded instructions found. The text is a 2026 arXiv preprint with forward-dated references. Model names (GPT-5.6, GLM-5.2, DeepSeek-V4, etc.) are as printed and I did not verify them. Table 2 text has an extraction glitch ("83.961.3" for JIT+V4-Flash, which is Shop 83.9 and Travel 61.3). Several figure bar-chart values came through as loose number lists; I relied on the text prose for those. The reference list was skimmed only. Pages read: 24 of 24.
